summary.summary: Oxfordshire took no new borrowing in 2025/26 and let £7m of debt go (a £2m PWLB maturity plus a £5m LOBO its lender called in November 2025), leaving £264.8m of borrowing against a £512.5m capital financing requirement — 48% internally funded — alongside £424m of investments. Treasury income beat budget by £8.2m on higher rates and balances, and the council parked the gains in reserves, including £8.0m added to a High Needs DSG risk reserve in June 2026. The shadow is the schools grant: the negative High Needs DSG balance reached £149.3m by year end, costing an estimated £6.0m in unearned interest this year (£16.4m cumulative since 2019/20) and steadily eating the cash the council can invest.

signals.headline: Negative High Needs DSG balance reached £149.3m by 31 March 2026; estimated £6.0m of unearned interest cost in 2025/26 (up from £3.8m in 2024/25), £16.4m cumulative since 2019/20
signals.why: The deficit behind the statutory override is consuming investable cash at an accelerating rate, and the council is pre-emptively parking £8m of treasury gains in a High Needs risk reserve against it.

signals.headline: A £5m LOBO at 3.68% was called and repaid without penalty on 24 November 2025; four LOBO loans totalling £20m remain
signals.why: Lenders have started exercising their options in this rate environment; the remaining £20m is modest against £424m of investments, so a further call is manageable.

signals.headline: No new external borrowing in 2025/26; debt down from £271.9m to £264.8m against a £512.5m CFR, with internal balances funding 48% of the requirement
signals.why: Shrinking external debt plus £424m of investments leaves little refinancing exposure — only 12.16% of borrowing matures within 12 months against a 20% limit.

news_drafts.headline: Oxfordshire's audit recovery stalls into third year after disclaimed opinion
news_drafts.lead: Oxfordshire County Council remains locked in multi-year audit recovery, with its accounts still unable to receive an unqualified sign-off three years after a complete audit failure. The auditors issued a disclaimer of opinion in 2023/24—the most serious form of audit failure—and a qualified opinion last year. Even by 2025/26, certain valuations and reserve movements will still lack assurance. The auditors have now flagged the council's General Fund Balance, a key measure of financial resilience, as presenting higher inherent risk due to material unaudited movements and susceptibility to management bias. They require confirmation that management can simultaneously rebuild historic records from 2022/23 onwards while delivering current-year audit work, and have signalled they will seek additional audit fees to reflect the scope of extra work required. Recovery remains on track for an unqualified opinion by 2026/27, but the pattern suggests underlying capacity constraints.

findings.committee: Thames Valley Fire Control Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix A Outturn Statement Qtr 1 2026-27 final including commentary
findings.headline: Committee forecast full-year underspend of £114,306 (3.66% of budget) driven by staff turnover savings exceeding grant income loss.
findings.detail: Thames Valley Fire Control Joint Committee forecasts total expenditure of £3,007,227 against a budget of £3,121,533, representing an underspend of £114,306. This underspend is driven primarily by staff turnover savings of £131,689, which exceed the combined impact of the £18,543 loss of grant income.
findings.matters: Overall budget position and how a joint committee balances multiple cost pressures demonstrates financial management capability relevant to lenders assessing sustainability.

findings.committee: Thames Valley Fire Control Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix A Outturn Statement Qtr 1 2026-27 final including commentary
findings.headline: Annual pay increase for uniform staff confirmed at 3.8%, exceeding budgeted estimate of 3%.
findings.detail: The annual pay increase for uniform staff has been confirmed at 3.8%, which is 0.8 percentage points above the budgeted estimate of 3%. The same revised rate, although not yet formally confirmed, was applied to forecast non-uniform staff pay awards.
findings.matters: Pay award settlements higher than budgeted represent cost pressures that affect all councils; finance directors track how peers manage pay settlements against budgets.
findings.figures: 3.8% uniform staff pay increase vs 3% budgeted; non-uniform rate not yet confirmed
findings.quote: The annual pay increase for uniform staff was confirmed at 3.8%, which is higher than budgeted estimate of 3%.

findings.committee: Thames Valley Fire Control Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix A Outturn Statement Qtr 1 2026-27 final including commentary
findings.headline: Forecast staff underspend of £131,689 due to turnover, with departing staff at top pay scales replaced by new starters at lowest rates.
findings.detail: The committee expects an underspend of £131,689 (5.73%) on employment costs due to staff turnover in Q4 2025/26 and Q1 2026/27. Leavers at the top of their pay scales have been replaced by new starters on the lowest rates of pay, with some posts having no salary cost during recruitment periods.
findings.matters: Material salary movements reflect how councils manage workforce planning through turnover cycles, affecting budget performance.
findings.quote: Due to staff turnover during Q4 2025/26 and Q1 2026/27, an underspend is now expected in this area. This results from leavers, who were all at the top of their pay scales, being replaced by new starters on the lowest rates of pay for their roles and periods whilst recruitment was taking place, where no salary was paid at all in respect of some posts.

findings.committee: Thames Valley Fire Control Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix A Outturn Statement Qtr 1 2026-27 final including commentary
findings.headline: Expected £19k grant relating to National Insurance increase will not be received in FY 2026/27, creating adverse variance of £18,543.
findings.detail: The committee budgeted to receive a grant relating to the National Insurance increase but will not receive it in FY 2026/27. Only MAIT grant of £10k was received against total grants budgeted at £28,803. This loss of expected government grant creates a material adverse variance.
findings.matters: Loss of anticipated grant income materially affects budget sustainability and indicates changing government funding for council services.
findings.figures: £19k grant not received; £10k MAIT grant received; £18,543 adverse variance (64.38% unfavourable)
findings.quote: MAIT grant received (£10k), however no grant relating to National Insurance increase (£19k) to be received in FY 2026/27, resulting in adverse variance.

findings.committee: Thames Valley Fire Control Joint Committee
findings.headline: Uniform staff pay award confirmed at 3.8%, exceeding budgeted assumption of 3%, already reflected in Q1 forecast
findings.detail: The annual pay award for uniform staff came in at 3.8% compared to 3% budgeted. This 0.8 percentage point overage has been incorporated into the Q1 forecast but will continue throughout the year.
findings.matters: Pay award overruns accumulate through the year; a baseline 0.8pp overage signals persistent cost pressure higher than originally anticipated for forward planning.
findings.figures: 3.8% actual pay award; 3% budgeted; 0.8 percentage point variance
findings.quote: The annual pay award for uniform staff was confirmed at 3.8%, compared to budgeted 3%, and is already reflected in the forecast.
